key_insight: Modeling a molecule as a conformational ensemble, rather than a single structure, substantially improves cyclic-peptide property prediction.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests that thermodynamically informed graph embeddings can boost molecular screening and design workflows for flexible biomolecules.
method: Encode each conformer with shared EGNN layers
Pool conformer embeddings with a Set Attention Block
Pretrain with masked-token recovery, noisy-coordinate reconstruction, and pairwise distance reconstruction
evidence_signal: On CREMP-CycPeptMPDB, the pretrained EnsembleEGNN achieved R^2=0.477 and Pearson r=0.699, outperforming a sequence-only BERT baseline (R^2=0.439, r=0.667), while training from scratch failed (R^2=0.005).
watch_item: Results are shown on cyclic peptides and may not transfer directly to other molecular families without careful validation of ensemble quality and computational cost.
paper_title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
